children: Data-center valuations have been on a rollercoaster ride recently as a backlash builds in some U.S. communities, including over their energy use and potential effect on power prices. Jefferies thinks Infratil's Longroad Energy business is less exposed to these headwinds than others. Longroad is continuing to work on a pipeline of 5 gigawatt opportunities. "As a renewable energy operator, Longroad can largely bring its own power, which may make approvals easier," analyst Roger Samuel says. "Its sites in Utah are not affected by the restrictions emerging elsewhere." Jefferies rates Infratil at "buy," and trims its price target by 1.6%, to NZ$18.20/share. Infratil is down 0.2%, to NZ$11.09/share, today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
